questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience living in Latin America and improve my spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was great, but unfortunately I did not feel super motivated by the classes I had (master student).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UDLAP is very helpful, but it is also important to ask around because for example the living situations are better outside UDLAP than on campus.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Possible to switch classes and professors were very flexible and helpful. There was a intro day with basic information about UDLAP

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is very very easy to find housing. I rented an airbnb for the first week and then found a housing the first week.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I did not realize how far Puebla is from Cholula, approximately 30 min in car. There are lots of housing options in Cholula and therefore only search for accommodations in Cholula. I payed 4000 pesos (1600 dkk) a month for a room in a house were I lived with 3 other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing was super nice but our landlord (Ray/Raymundo/Cholula Capital) wanted to host parties and our house for all students which felt weird, but he respected us saying no. This is not a reason to completely avoid Cholula Capital housings if you for example like partying a lot. There are other companies that offer housings without hosting parties at your house, for example Charro Housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its a different system than UCPH and you only register for classes very short time before starting to study.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to wish for classes a couple of days before you start and then you get notified very shortly before the classes begin, which ones you got

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a "international office" in UDLAP which helped, also if you wanted to change courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every class I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose the classes you find most interesting and change if it does not work for you

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of options for MA students

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Workload is not very big, since most of MA students at UDLAP has a job while studying. MA courses are only 2 hours a week, but they do take attendance. You decide yourself if you want to attend online or in person, most students attend online (maybe only 1-3 are there in class)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller courses (10-25 people).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Statistics in business
International finance
Business Economics (microeconomics and macroeconomics)
Business Intelligence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend choosing courses in Spanish if you want to improve.

questions.answer: I did not cook a lot of meals at home, so dinning out

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was cheaper than I expected, food is not that cheap, data on your sim card is not that cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tennis court, basketball court, football fields, swimming pool and gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the facilities a UDLAP

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do some of the hikes on the dormant volcanoes around Cholula (La Malinche and iztaccíhuatl). Visit other cities and states in Mexico

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It felt like home very quickly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are more open than Danish people and will probably approach you

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly language barrier, but they were very patient with my bad Spanish in my experience

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people, the food and the nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try and learn a bit of Spanish
Mexico felt super safe and especially Cholula so dont be nervous at all
Unless you find courses that really interest you, the reason to go here probably should not be academic only. The best part was experiencing the country

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Order groceries with uber eats. There are no supermarkets close to UDLAP, only small "tiendas".

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with people from all over the world and learning Spanish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
